title: A long tool call must not look like silence: observe-only PRE hook + tool-in-flight state

defect.observed: the watchdog HELD the mpd-default team with cause {kind:'silence', ms:131049} on an in_progress task whose owner was running a real-boot lane, not wedged
defect.mechanism: the heartbeat stamped on model steps and on tool COMPLETION only (W-9), so any tool call longer than warnSilenceMs was indistinguishable from a wedge
defect.class: false positive (a healthy team paused), the same class as the t71/t73/t79 repairs, reached through a different door

dists.note: the pre-fix bytes were COPIED into the evidence directory BEFORE the rebuild, so the BEFORE half of the measurement runs the real pre-fix plugin, not a reconstruction; both dists are newer than every source file under their packages (checked with find -newer)

design.pre_hook: adapter.onPreToolExecute(listener) wraps the harness's tools/pre-execute WATERFALL, owns next(), returns the downstream decision VERBATIM and discards the listener's return value; the listener observes a FROZEN SHALLOW COPY of the execution, so it can neither mutate what will be dispatched nor affect the gate; a throwing listener is contained; no event bus -> no-op
design.stamps: tool-start (PRE, carries tool + callId) opens a call; tool (POST, completion, unchanged W-9 semantics) closes it; matched by callId
design.state: the in-flight fact is derived from the durable heartbeat JSONL, so it survives a process restart
design.predicate: machine.observe treats an OPEN call younger than toolInFlightMaxMs as explained activity (no WARN, no ESCALATE, streak reset); past the bound it emits ONE tool-expired decision per task+attempt
design.tool_expired_action: durable WARN-class incident only: scene null, hold not-requested, never a scene, never a hold, never an escalate
design.failure_mode: a member wedged INSIDE a hanging tool is reported once past the bound and never escalated/paused; stated in the README and the plugin source
design.cross_scope_edits: none: packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin, packages/mpd-bundle-plugin, skills/**, docs/**, VENDOR_LOCK.json and .mpd/** are untouched (--check still reports 53 regions across 9 adopted files)

The adapter's observe-only PRE hook (`onPreToolExecute` → `tools/pre-execute`) now stamps `tool-start` with the harness `callId`, the POST stamp closes it, and the silence predicate treats an OPEN call younger than `watchdog.toolInFlightMaxMs` (default 15 min, `0` disables) as explained activity. not_claimed: No live `dsh` host and no model turn were booted here: the real long command is a genuine child process dispatched through the real cordis waterfall and the real adapter, but the surrounding harness tool registry is modelled on the dispatch order measured in dsh-tools (gate -> body -> post-execute).

The THROW/CANCEL lifecycle claim rests on the installed harness source, not on a live host: `dsh-tools/lib/index.js:3203-3207` states tool and unknown-tool failures still receive post-execute (so a throwing tool clears its own entry) while pipeline failures are final (no POST -> the bound applies). The fixture proves the POST-clears-it half; the no-POST half is proven by the bound case.
The 15-minute default is a chosen bound, not a measured optimum; the knob is live-tunable and `0` disables the rule.

The 2 failures in the in-repo `bun test packages` run are NOT this task's: they are mpd-config tests asserting on this workspace's `.mpd/mpd.jsonc` (the captain's temporary file); the same 731 tests are green from a clean cwd, and the failing file alone is 21/2 in-repo vs 23/0 from a clean cwd.
W-3 stands: no genuine provider wedge is reproduced anywhere in this evidence.
